run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:52:31Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: RequestErrorRate is firing for otel-demo/frontend-proxy because the request path frontend-proxy -> frontend -> cart hangs and frontend-proxy cuts its clients off at its 15 s route timeout. From about 01:51 the cart service lost its redis backing store: cart server spans 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' ran 468-480 s and then returned FailedPrecondition "Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis" (EnsureRedisConnected, ValkeyCartStore.cs:97); frontend answered HTTP 500 on /api/cart and POST /api/cart; frontend-proxy logged HTTP 504 "UT response_timeout" with response time 15000 ms against upstream cluster frontend. frontend-proxy's ingress error-span rate sat at 0-0.011/s through the 01:51:31 sample, rose to 0.178/s at 01:52:31, and peaked near 1.46/s at 01:58-02:01, matching the alert's 1.0889 and its 01:52:31 start. The fault is located at valkey-cart rather than at cart because a second, independent client of that server (otel-collector's redisreceiver) also lost it: all four redis metrics it exports last advanced at the 01:51:00 sample and were exactly frozen through 02:00:00 while the same collector kept updating every other metric. The valkey-cart pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, cgroup memory failcnt 0, and only mild CPU throttling, so why valkey stopped answering is not established; its CPU limit of 10m and memory limit of 10Mi are a plausible pre-existing fragility but not a proven trigger, and the change history that would show what happened at 01:51 is not integrated. Conclusion partial: failing path and faulty dependency established, in-valkey mechanism unresolved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error-span rate for span_name=ingress, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 to 0.011/s in the samples from 01:35:31 to 01:51:31, then 0.1778/s at 01:52:31, 0.5667/s at 01:53:31, 0.948/s at 01:54:31 and 1.4407-1.4629/s in the 01:57:31-02:01:31 samples; the deviation begins exactly at the alert's 01:52:31 firing minute, while the earlier blips up to 0.011/s were stable background.

At 15 s steps the frontend-proxy error rate oscillates between 0 and bursts of about 3.0-3.5/s from 01:50 to 02:01 (e.g. 1.6 at 01:52:00, 3.5 at 01:53:00, 3.2667 at 01:55:00, 3.0667 at 01:59:00, 3.4 at 02:01:00), while cart and frontend error spans in the same series are only 0.1-0.37/s, i.e. far fewer failing client requests than proxy ingress errors.

The frontend-proxy container access log shows HTTP 504 with response flag "UT response_timeout" and response time 15000 ms against upstream cluster "frontend" for GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, GET /api/checkout and POST /api/checkout, e.g. 'GET /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 0 24 14999 ... frontend' at collected timestamp 2026-11-17T01:58:29Z.

Traces show cart server spans 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' with otel.status_code ERROR and status description 'FailedPrecondition ... Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() ... ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 97'; those spans started around 01:51:47-01:51:51 and lasted 468.2-479.7 s (duration_us 468183414-479682021).

In the same traces frontend spans return http.status_code 500 on 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' after 489.9-501.2 s with message '9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis', propagated through client spans 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' (rpc.grpc.status_code=9), while frontend-proxy ingress spans on those traces record http.status_code 504 at ~15.0 s.

The cart container log of pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 repeats 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' (67 matching lines in the 01:58-01:59 range alone) alongside the gRPC wrapper line 'Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised.', whose earliest retained occurrence is 2026-11-17T01:53:24Z.

The redis metrics otel-collector's redisreceiver exports for valkey-cart stopped advancing at the 01:51:00 sample and held identical values through 02:00:00: redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="sys"} frozen at 1.704472, redis_memory_used_bytes frozen at 1710360, redis_memory_fragmentation_ratio frozen at 5.71, redis_memory_rss_bytes frozen at 9744384, while the same collector's span metrics and the kubelet container metrics kept updating.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is phase Running with ready=true, restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated reason, and pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 likewise; both started at 2026-11-17T01:19:19Z, before the 01:51 deviation, and both run on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae.

Dependency discovery is intact: the Endpoints object for service valkey-cart lists address 100.96.2.228 on port 6379, and cart, frontend and frontend-proxy Endpoints each list one address (100.96.2.233, 100.96.3.244, 100.96.2.115) on port 8080; the cart deployment sets env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379.
No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace otel-demo at query time (query returned an empty list), so no policy-based block between cart and valkey-cart is visible in the cluster objects.

The valkey-cart container's cgroup memory failcnt is 0 in every sample from 01:31 to 02:05 and its working set stayed 3.49-4.33 MB against a 10Mi limit, so no memory-limit reclaim or OOM is recorded for valkey-cart; cart's container working set grew from ~57.5 MB to ~95.9 MB against a 165Mi limit.

CPU throttling is far larger on the caller than on the dependency: cart-755465879b-t9mf7 container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total rate was ~0.8-1.9/s before onset and rose to 4.60/s (01:54), 7.24/s (01:55) and 6.27-8.44/s (01:57-02:00), while valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr stayed at 0.04-0.45/s and its CPU usage moved only from ~0.0045 to ~0.0066 cores against a 10m limit.

The 01:52:31 deviation is confined to the cart path and its callers: error-span rates are zero for accounting, payment, currency, shipping, email, fraud-detection and product-catalog (ad and fraud-detection show only ~0.0037/s flagd EventStream background), while error spans appear on cart 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', frontend '/api/cart', 'POST /api/cart', '/api/checkout' and checkout 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' / 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' from the 01:54:31 sample; in the sampled traces product-catalog 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' still returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in 104-129 us.
All five cluster nodes report Ready=True with no other condition true at query time, including i-0146cb0d0caf26bae which hosts both cart-755465879b-t9mf7 and valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr.

The only otel-demo events in the window concern pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s, which is not the current cart pod: 75 Normal 'Killing' (Stopping container cart, 2026-11-17T01:55:21Z) and 30 Warning 'FailedKillPod' with 'failed to "KillContainer" ... DeadlineExceeded' (01:55:20Z); the serving cart Endpoint is only 100.96.2.233 (cart-755465879b-t9mf7), so this terminating leftover is not in the request path.

Every fault-injection flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (including cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) is at its "off" defaultVariant in the object read at query time, so no flag-declared fault is enabled now; the ConfigMap shows current state only and cannot prove its state at 01:51.

frontend-proxy is not where the fault originates: its client spans 'router frontend egress' carry http.status_code 200 on the successful traces and its metrics series for that span carries STATUS_CODE_UNSET in every sample, and its failing ingress spans are 504s emitted only after the 15 s route timeout while the upstream frontend request kept running for about 500 s; the frontend in turn failed only on cart RPCs, with FAILED_PRECONDITION text originating in valkey.

The cart error increase is not explained by cart being restarted, rescheduled or OOM-killed: cart-755465879b-t9mf7 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no last-terminated reason, and its memory working set (~57-96 MB) stays below its 165Mi limit throughout.

A cluster-wide node or policy cause is not supported: all nodes are Ready with no pressure conditions, no NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo, all otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and the services that did show error spans outside the cart path are limited to cart's callers plus checkout's cart calls, not other dependencies.

Rejected: that a memory-limit OOM or container restart of valkey-cart explains the outage. Its cgroup memory failcnt stayed 0 with working set ~3.5-4.3 MB against a 10Mi limit, the pod shows restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated reason, and the only Warning event in the window is FailedKillPod on the unrelated terminating pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s.

Rejected as the trigger: a rollout or reschedule of cart or valkey-cart during the window. The serving pods cart-755465879b-t9mf7 and valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr both started at 2026-11-17T01:19:19Z with restartCount 0; the 01:55 Killing/FailedKillPod events name cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s, a pod of a ReplicaSet that is no longer current and that is not a cart Service endpoint, so they record cleanup of a leftover pod (with a kubelet kill timeout) rather than a change to the serving workload.

Hypothesis (unproven, kept open): valkey-cart's tiny CPU limit of 10m (Deployment valkey-cart pod template, about 2x its observed 4.5-6.6m usage) starves the redis event loop so cart connections and the collector's redis scrape time out. Supporting: throttled periods are non-zero throughout (0.04-0.45/s), i.e. about 0.4-4.5% of CFS periods. Weakening: the throttling rate does not step up before onset (0.185/s at 01:51, 0.220/s at 01:52) and the pod template dates from 01:19:19Z, so this setting predates the incident and would be a pre-existing fragility, not the change that triggered it.

Hypothesis (unproven, kept open): the valkey-cart redis process itself became wedged or stopped accepting connections at about 01:51, for a reason not visible in the collected evidence (for example a blocking persistence fork or internal stall). Supporting: all four redis INFO-derived series freeze at the same 01:51:00 sample while the same collector keeps every other metric fresh, and cart fails inside EnsureRedisConnected. Nothing collected identifies the internal mechanism; valkey-cart's log stream returned no lines and its redis configuration could not be read.

Hypothesis (unproven, kept open): a configuration change applied around 01:51 to valkey-cart or cart (env, limits or redis settings) made the dependency stop answering. Current objects show VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and the 10m/10Mi limits, but the change-history integration is not available in this Run, so a change at 01:51 can neither be confirmed nor excluded.

Inspect the valkey-cart container directly (redis-cli PING/INFO clients,stats,memory and LATENCY DOCTOR, plus its effective redis.conf: maxmemory, maxclients, save/appendonly) since its log stream is empty and its redis INFO-derived metrics have been frozen since 01:51; a PING that hangs inside the container would confirm a server-side stall rather than a cart-side client problem.

Raise the valkey-cart container limits (currently cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) toward the upstream otel-demo values, add a readiness probe and a real redis health check, then re-measure container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total and redis metric freshness; this addresses the CPU-starvation hypothesis and removes a single-point fragility regardless of the eventual trigger.

Bound the cart-to-valkey calls in time (client connect/sync timeouts and a gRPC deadline inside ValkeyCartStore) so a redis stall fails fast instead of holding frontend requests for about 500 s; that keeps frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout from converting one dependency stall into 504s and would have capped the 8-minute hangs seen in the traces.

Add an alert on valkey-cart redis metric staleness (for example redis_cpu_time_seconds_total not increasing for 5 minutes) so loss of the cart datastore is signalled before the frontend-proxy request-error alert, and separately check the leftover pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s whose deletion keeps failing with FailedKillPod on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00.

gaps: No valkey-cart container log lines were retrievable for the window: the valkey-cart log query returned no lines and status no_data for both current and previous container instance, so the redis-side view of the stall is unknown.

The effective redis configuration of valkey-cart (maxmemory, maxclients, persistence, blocked clients) cannot be read: its deployment has no command/args or ConfigMap mount, and secrets cannot be read.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether any Deployment/ConfigMap/env change was applied to valkey-cart or cart at about 01:51 cannot be verified; pod start times (01:19:19Z) only show the current pods predate onset.

The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not found in the target rule groups (list_prometheus_rules by rule_name returned nothing, status no_data), so its expression, labels and 'for' duration could not be confirmed and the reported value 1.0889 could not be recomputed.

The final step of the rate series is 0 for every series including total throughput at 02:05:31 with data_as_of 02:05:31, which is consistent with a data/scrape gap rather than recovery; incident state after about 02:04 is unknown.

The queries for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason, container_network_receive_packets_total and container_fs_usage_bytes produced no series (status no_data), and no redis_* series beyond the six listed names exist, so container restart history, pod network activity and disk usage for valkey-cart could not be assessed; these are unknown, not zero.

Cart log lines before 2026-11-17T01:53:24Z were not present in the readable stream, so the first redis failure cannot be timestamped from logs; the earliest observed failure point is the cart span starting about 01:51:50 plus the 01:51:00 redis metric freeze.

A trace search for service 'cart' in 01:55-02:02 returned no data while an error-tagged cart search in 01:50-02:05 returned traces, so trace coverage of the later window is incomplete; spans shown are a sample of the service and operation they came from, not a complete call chain.

Why the leftover pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s could not be killed by kubelet (FailedKillPod, DeadlineExceeded on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00) is unexplained and no evidence ties it to the cart/redis failure.

Health of services outside the cart path (ad, currency, shipping, email, payment, image-provider, recommendation, quote, accounting, kafka) rests on their error-span rates only; their logs and latencies were not examined, so they are checked for errors but not fully cleared.
next_steps: Have an operator exec into pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr and run PING, INFO stats/clients/memory and LATENCY DOCTOR to determine whether the server is stalled, and read its effective configuration.
Check the valkey-cart container's runtime state on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (containerd/crictl inspect, D-state processes, dmesg OOM events) to see whether the process is blocked in the kernel.

Obtain the change history for namespace otel-demo (Deployments valkey-cart and cart, ConfigMap flagd-config) around 2026-11-17T01:45-01:52Z from the change-management system, since that integration was unavailable here.
Retrieve the Prometheus/Alertmanager rule definition for RequestErrorRate to confirm its expression and threshold against the observed 1.0889.
Re-query a fresh window after 02:04Z to establish whether the incident persisted or cleared, since the last returned sample looks like a data gap rather than a recovery.
